Emma —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a draft MAP and a lightweight token model (CSV) that implements three scenarios: baseline, optimistic (+caching/prefetch), and stress. High-level notes here so procurement/engineering can scan quickly: 

1) Baseline assumptions (conservative):
   - Avg request: 420 tokens (prompt + expected generated content)
   - Tokenization: standard UTF-8 tokenization (~1.9 chars/token for your dataset)
   - Batching: typical batching target 6 requests per GPU batch during normal traffic (reduces tokens/second cost by ~18% vs no batching)
   - Caching: prefix reuse assumed 18% for templated prompts (customer-specific)
   - Quantization: we model both 8-bit and 4-bit variants; baseline uses 8-bit with small perf penalty

2) Optimistic (what we tune towards in evaluation):
   - Batching = 10 reqs/batch average (peak-friendly), Caching = 30% reuse, syntax-level prefetch for common completions
   - Expected unit cost improvement: ~25–35% vs baseline in model run cost (tokens/$) depending on sequence length distribution

3) Stress (tail case):
   - Peak QPS with low batching (1–2 reqs/batch) + low caching (5%) — unit cost increases up to 2.4x baseline; we show monthly spend at several QPS points in the CSV.

MAP / evaluation plan (short):
- Week 0 (sign): finalize dataset / canonical eval prompts; Redwood provides MAP_v2.xlsx with checkpoints.
- Week 1: run token-cost smoke tests (short synthetic and sampled production traces). Acceptance: model unit cost within 20% of baseline model in the sheet.
- Week 2: tune batching/caching knobs on a 2-day performance window; measure qps-to-latency tradeoffs.
- Week 3: run 72-hour sustained load to validate tail behavior and cost sensitivity.
- Week 4: finalize report and sign-off for production pilot.

A few asks for you so we can populate the stress table accurately:
- Typical session length distribution (p50/p90 tokens) or a sampled CSV of 500 representative traces.
- Target SLA (p95 latency) and whether you prefer lower latency or lower cost as the tradeoff.

I attached MAP_LumoCare_v2.xlsx and redwood_token_model.csv (the CSV has example QPS rows so you can slide numbers). If it's helpful, Ben can add a short appendix on prefetch/batch heuristics.

Connor / Neha —

Quick technical notes to drop into the MAP appendix (I'll sign off on this before we send to Emma):

- Batching: continuous batching with a 10–15 ms collection window gives the best latency/cost tradeoff for interactive apps. If LumoCare's p50 inter-arrival is >40ms, target 8–12 reqs/batch. If inter-arrival is bursty with <10ms p50, reduce collection window and accept slightly lower batching efficacy.

- Caching: distinguish prefix-only caching vs full-response caching. Prefix caching (templates + small user context) is high-return for LumoCare because many calls are repetitive. We should instrument prefix hit-rate early (first 48 hours).

- Prefetch: prefetching top-K likely completions for common prompts reduces end-to-end latency but increases token churn; only enable in optimistic runs.

- Quantization fallback: run 4-bit on tail-heavy long-sequence flows for cost control; validate quality degradation on eval set (expect ~2–3% drop in exact-match for code-like completions, smaller for free-text).

- Acceptance thresholds suggestion for MAP gating:
   * Unit cost (tokens per USD) within 30% of model sheet baseline under Week 2 tuned settings.
   * Peak p95 latency under the requested SLA when using recommended batching settings.

I'll prepare a 1-page appendix with sample scripts to collect prefix-hit-rate and a short notebook to reproduce the stress scenarios in the CSV.

Ben
